title: Anganwadi workers: the first face of the State for a child
author: Editorial Desk
summary: Millions of children, pregnant women and mothers are reached by the ICDS through a woman from their own village.
body:
The **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)** began in 1975. It offers supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, immunisation, health check-ups and referral services to children under six and to pregnant and nursing women. The centre where all this happens is the **Anganwadi**.

## Who runs it

Each centre has an **Anganwadi worker (AWW)** and a **helper**. They keep records, weigh children, give hot cooked meals and take-home rations, visit homes and often mobilise the village for health campaigns. In recent years they have also been asked to use mobile apps for data entry.

## Common demands

- A higher **honorarium** and its regular payment.
- **Recognition as workers**, rather than as volunteers.
- **Pension and gratuity** on retirement.
- Relief from heavy **digital reporting** without proper phones or data.
- **Promotion** opportunities, including to supervisor posts.

## The BMS angle

BMS-affiliated organisations of Anganwadi workers have sent memoranda to ministers and joined demonstrations in many States. BMS argues that these women are part of the nation-building chain from the first thousand days of life, and that the State must recognise their work.

## A fact to remember

The work is not only data. It is trust. A mother who has not been to a clinic will often listen to the Anganwadi sister.
